entries.what: Primitives & reusable atoms: UUID, ISO-8601 DateTime, hex color, URI, lowercase-hyphen Slug, SemVer, user reference, rich-text spans, asset metadata, dataset, axis config. Every other plugin in the projection composes from this layer.
entries.why: Single source of truth for shared primitive validation; downstream plugins depend on these atoms and validators.

entries.what: Generic patch engine: validate(doc), patch(original, partial) with deep merge and immutable field protection, computeDiff producing structural DiffEntry[], applyArrayOps for id-resolved insert/remove/move/update, batched cross-entity transactions with rollback.
entries.why: Encodes the patchable-first convention that makes every other schema surgically editable. Without this plugin, edits would be replace-only.

entries.what: SemVer 2.0.0-based version tracking: ParsedSemVer { major, minor, patch, prerelease?, build? }, optimistic locking metadata, snapshot history, and structured comparable version metadata that replaces ad-hoc integer counters.
entries.why: Standard, comparable version metadata for any schema, template, or content entity. Every long-lived primitive type needs this.

entries.what: Implementation profile for Bridge Theory: overlap typing (equivalence, subsumption, constraint, derivation, independent), bridge relations (causal etc.), and slug/uuid/semver-typed identity for cross-domain conceptual mapping.
entries.why: Reusable schema for declaring relationships between two formal models or domains. B-tier because demand for cross-domain bridge declarations is unproven.

entries.what: Canonical theme/tokens object for colors, typography, spacing, radius, breakpoints. Includes a DTCG-aligned token model (DesignTokenLeaf with $type/$value, recursive DesignTokenGroup) and named token collections (core, semantic, components, modes, platforms).
entries.why: Foundation for pixel-consistent rendering across presentation and CMS surfaces. Every renderer depends on this.

entries.what: Cross-surface rendering policy: ImagePlacement (fit, alignment, focal point, crop, safe area), RenderProfile contract (surface kind, density, unit system, motion, color mode), RenderProfileSet with optional default-profile id.
entries.why: A single contract that lets the same content render pixel-consistently across slides, pages, and templates.

entries.what: Discriminated transform-target schema (SurfaceSchema slide_deck/page_layout, WebsiteSchema website) that constrains which frame types are valid per surface kind, plus the SemVer-stamped transform profile metadata.
entries.why: Encodes which transforms are legal between which schemas, preventing mismatched surface/frame combinations at validate time instead of at render time.

entries.what: Structured documents composed of typed Blocks (text, heading, image, chart, table, list, quote, code, callout, embed, divider) grouped into Sections and bundled into a Content document with provenance fields.
entries.why: Content authored once here projects into many surfaces (slides, pages, templates).

entries.what: Slide deck schema: Slides compose by SlotBindings that point to ContentPointers (entire section, single block, range of blocks, or inline-only deck content), with per-slide overrides and animations.
entries.why: Separates content authorship from presentation; the same content can drive many decks.

entries.what: Branded landing-page schema: 22 PageSection variants (hero, manifesto, value proposition, services, competitive positioning, voice & tone, etc.) with discriminated union, per-section AI context, and primary plus additional content-source tracking.
entries.why: Encodes the marketing/brand surface so the same content tree can feed many sites.

entries.what: Universal CMS plugin: SectionTemplate (versioned), recursive FieldDefinition (slots and union variants), SectionInstance/Page/Site composition, hardcoded primitive field values (text/richtext/number/boolean/color/enum/date + media + currency), hierarchical TaxonomyTerm with helpers, runtime per-template/per-field validation, computed-field expression resolver, template-version migrations, and TypeScript-interface codegen for known templates.
entries.why: Section types are SectionTemplate definitions with recursive FieldDefinition trees, not hard-coded code — growth happens via templates, not enums. The eight source files (definitions, field-values, taxonomy, validation, computed, migrations, typegen, index) are facets of one plugin in any sane packaging.
notes: Prior revision listed these 8 files as 9 separate plugin entries (counting both the root barrel and the internal index). They are one plugin with eight modules; splitting them would force consumers to install eight packages to get a working CMS.

entries.what: Layered AI context plugin: three-scope inheritance (Site → Section → Field), AgentPersona / Audience / FieldAIHints / SectionAIContext / SurfaceAIContext / FrameAIContext / SlotAIContext schemas, voice/tone enrichments (VocabularyLevel, FormalityLevel, WritingPrinciple, PersonaVoiceVariant, VoiceGuidelines), DB-backed PromptTemplate (slug-keyed, organization-scoped, non-technical-editable), and the resolveAIContext + buildSystemPrompt runtime that emits a structured system prompt with policy and behavioural-execution constraints.
entries.why: Turns 'fill in a string' into 'write a 6-word headline for enterprise CTOs avoiding the word leverage'. Encodes intent (audience, tone, banned words, quality criteria) as data, not hand-written prompts. The mixin/context/generation/runtime split exists for source-file ergonomics, not packaging.
notes: ai-agent-mixin-usage.ts is a runnable demo and lives in the inventory file as kind: "demo".

entries.what: Reusable UI copy patterns: MessagePattern (template + tone + max length), EmptyStatePattern (headline + body + action + illustration), CTAPattern (verb choices + length + caps rules), ConfirmationDialogPattern (with destructive flag), FeedbackPattern (toast/alert with duration and dismissibility), bundled into MicrocopyPatterns and exposed as a spread MicrocopyMixin.
entries.why: Standardised UI copy primitives that prevent each surface from inventing its own message conventions.

entries.what: i18n configuration: PluralizationConfig (zero-one-other / one-other / ordinal / custom rules), InterpolationConfig (braces / doubleBraces / percent / dollar variable syntax), full LocalizationConfig with locales, fallback, RTL, date/number formatting, plus a LocalizationMixin spread.
entries.why: Lets any schema declare its locale/formatting/pluralization expectations in one place.

entries.what: RBAC model: DataScope (own/team/org/global), RoleDefinition (named role with inheritance, default and admin flags), PermissionDefinition (categorised), FeatureEntitlement (plan-gated with limits and upsell), DataScopeRule (per-entity visibility with conditions), PermissionUIBehavior, all bundled into PermissionsModel.
entries.why: Standard RBAC primitives so feature entitlements, roles, and data scopes are not reinvented per app.

entries.what: Structured AI-assisted session-journaling schema: ContinuityJournal entries with stop-reasons (discriminated union), files-of-interest, branch state, weighted observations, and explicit next-step lists, designed to minimise context loss between coding sessions.
entries.why: Captures the 'why', not just the 'what', of a working session so the next session can resume cleanly. B-tier because adoption depends on workflow discipline — this is a shipping plugin candidate, not an obvious win.

entries.what: Feature catalogue schema: FeatureStatus (draft / in_development / feature_flagged / ga / deprecated / removed), DependencyType (required / optional / conflicts), Hint probes (class / method / regex) that confirm a file is genuinely linked to a feature, plus AI-teaching metadata via the zod-ai-meta utility.
entries.why: Treats features as first-class, machine-checkable entities with status, dependencies, and code-link probes — the kind of artefact that survives reorgs.
notes: The zod-ai-meta library it depends on is a utility in the inventory file, not its own plugin.

entries.what: Framework formalisation plugin: registers a single profile (cap:profile) for canvas-style frameworks plus a validator (cap:validator) that runs the per-framework superRefine cross-checks. Ships a built-in catalogue of 71 frameworks — BMC, VPC, St. Gallen, Platform vs Pipeline, Porter Five Forces, Porter Generic Strategies, JTBD (Christensen, Ulwick), Lean Startup, Blue Ocean, Seven Powers, Dynamic Capabilities, DDBM (Hartmann/Zaki/Feldmann/Neely), Four Box, Wardley Mapping, plus the long tail of strategy/AI-economics/ governance/ethics frameworks. New frameworks are added as catalogue data, not as new plugins.
entries.why: All 71 source files share the same architectural shape (enums + atoms → item schemas → root model schema → portfolio schema, with patchable-first identified arrays and superRefine cross-checks). Splitting them into 71 plugins forced the prior revision to invent a Tier-B label for the long tail and produced a registry where the framework family dominated by sheer file count rather than by FDPM-specific value. One plugin + a parameter (which framework set to load) is the right packaging.
notes: Source: concept-design/schemas/business-models/*.ts (71 framework files + shared.ts utility + framework-list.ts catalogue + index.ts barrel).
Per-framework formalisations are catalogued in concept-schemas-inventory.ts as kind: "data" entries (one per framework), each linking to its source file.
The framework catalogue is not a closed enum — new frameworks are added by appending to the catalogue, not by issuing a new plugin.

entries.what: Design Token Community Group (DTCG) interop: import/export DesignTokenLeaf trees as DTCG-compliant JSON, normalise vendor-specific extensions, and round-trip with the canonical fdpm.design-system token model.
entries.why: DTCG is the only cross-vendor interop format for design tokens (Figma Tokens, Style Dictionary, Tokens Studio). Shipping the adapter as a separable plugin avoids forcing every design-system consumer to take the DTCG dependency.
notes: Implementation surface: derived from the DTCG sections of concept-design/schemas/design-system.ts; would be split into its own module on packaging.

entries.what: Brand identity bundle: ships a single coherent set of tokens, microcopy patterns, voice/tone, and AI-context defaults as one installable pack. Composes design-system + microcopy + ai-agent-context defaults.
entries.why: The most common consumer ask is 'give me a starter brand', not 'let me wire 4 plugins together'. A meta-plugin that ships defaults across the three layers is a real packaging unit, not a reach.
notes: Implementation surface: synthesised from design-system + microcopy + ai-context defaults; explicitly NOT in the source archive yet (the archive ships per-layer schemas, not a packaged bundle). Listed here as a real packaging candidate, called out as new in notes.
New entry vs prior revision — was implicit in the design-system + microcopy + ai-context combination but never named.

entries.what: TypeScript-interface codegen plugin: walks a registered cap:profile and emits a TypeScript declaration so consumers can opt into compile-time type checks for known templates while keeping the runtime flexibility of the universal schema.
entries.why: The site-schema plugin's typegen module is useful for any profile, not just SectionTemplate. Promoting it to a standalone plugin lets non-CMS profiles use it without taking the CMS dependency.
notes: Source: concept-design/schemas/site-schema/typegen.ts (extracted from the universal-CMS plugin in this revision).

entries.why: Logs convert vague reports into diagnosable evidence
entries.sourceSection: Domain profiles — Customer Service / Support Operations

entries.what: Link from service case to engineering issue, bug, incident, or backlog item
entries.why: Support-to-engineering handoff is a common failure point
entries.sourceSection: Domain profiles — Customer Service / Support Operations

entries.what: Product release, deployment, migration, or config change related to service demand
entries.why: Release context explains sudden contact spikes and regressions
entries.sourceSection: Domain profiles — Customer Service / Support Operations

entries.what: Public or internal status-page incident associated with customer cases
entries.why: Status pages coordinate customer messaging and incident linkage
entries.sourceSection: Domain profiles — Customer Service / Support Operations

entries.what: Reference to stock, part, device, replacement unit, or warehouse state
entries.why: Hardware and retail support need inventory-aware resolution
entries.sourceSection: Domain profiles — Customer Service / Support Operations

entries.what: Carrier, tracking, delivery exception, address validation, and delivery proof reference
entries.why: Shipping issues require external state and evidence
entries.sourceSection: Domain profiles — Customer Service / Support Operations

entries.what: Reference to payment processor event, authorization, dispute, or settlement
entries.why: Payment disputes require provider evidence and timelines
entries.sourceSection: Domain profiles — Customer Service / Support Operations

entries.what: Reference to SSO, IAM, password reset, MFA, or account access event
entries.why: Access support depends on identity-system evidence
entries.sourceSection: Domain profiles — Customer Service / Support Operations

entries.what: Reference to device health report, firmware, serial number, or diagnostic bundle
entries.why: Device support needs machine evidence tied to the customer case
entries.sourceSection: Domain profiles — Customer Service / Support Operations

entries.what: Reference to IoT device twin, state shadow, commands, and telemetry
entries.why: Connected-device support requires current and historical device state
entries.sourceSection: Domain profiles — Customer Service / Support Operations

entries.what: Case opened with vendor, partner, carrier, supplier, or outsourced provider
entries.why: Customer support often depends on external parties and their SLAs
entries.sourceSection: Domain profiles — Customer Service / Support Operations

entries.what: Structured transfer to partner or outsourced team with context and obligations
entries.why: External handoff needs stronger context packaging and accountability
entries.sourceSection: Domain profiles — Customer Service / Support Operations

entries.what: Performance, quality, SLA, and compliance metrics for BPO or partner teams
entries.why: Outsourced service needs visibility equivalent to internal teams
entries.sourceSection: Domain profiles — Customer Service / Support Operations

entries.what: External event ingested into the service workspace with signature and replay metadata
entries.why: Event-driven support needs reliable integration records
entries.sourceSection: Domain profiles — Customer Service / Support Operations

entries.what: Service-platform API call record relevant to automation, sync, or customer action
entries.why: Integration debugging needs request-level traceability
entries.sourceSection: Domain profiles — Customer Service / Support Operations

entries.what: Failed synchronization with CRM, billing, order, identity, or knowledge systems
entries.why: Sync failures create incorrect context and bad customer outcomes
entries.sourceSection: Domain profiles — Customer Service / Support Operations

entries.what: Field mapping between service objects and external systems
entries.why: Mappings are operational contracts and drift over time
entries.sourceSection: Domain profiles — Customer Service / Support Operations

entries.what: Conflict between systems of record for customer, account, entitlement, or product data
entries.why: Data conflicts are a frequent cause of wrong service decisions
entries.sourceSection: Domain profiles — Customer Service / Support Operations

entries.what: Declared authoritative source for a field, object, or decision
entries.why: Service agents need to know which data wins when systems disagree
entries.sourceSection: Domain profiles — Customer Service / Support Operations

entries.what: Retry, backoff, idempotency, dead-letter, and replay rules for service integrations
entries.why: Integration reliability depends on explicit retry semantics
entries.sourceSection: Domain profiles — Customer Service / Support Operations

entries.what: Export package of service records for customer, regulator, legal, audit, or analytics use
entries.why: Exports need scoping, redaction, approval, and traceability
entries.sourceSection: Domain profiles — Customer Service / Support Operations

entries.what: Imported service history, tickets, contacts, or knowledge from another platform
entries.why: Migration and consolidation require provenance for imported records
entries.sourceSection: Domain profiles — Customer Service / Support Operations

entries.what: Synthetic or test case used for training, QA, automation, or integration testing
entries.why: Test data prevents production records from being abused for experiments
entries.sourceSection: Domain profiles — Customer Service / Support Operations

entries.what: Service-platform environment such as production, staging, sandbox, or training
entries.why: Automation and tests must not confuse environments
